newsitem.title: USA: Regulators approve SBC, Telesis merger.
newsitem.headline: Regulators approve SBC, Telesis merger.

text.p: California regulators on Monday approved SBC Communications Inc's $17 billion merger with Pacific Telesis Group on the condition that customers receive a $341 million refund.

The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) was the only regulatory body whose approval of the merger was still needed. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission approved the merger plan earlier this year. The commission said Pacific Telesis' Pacific Bell unit would issue the refund to ratepayers over five years beginning in 1998 to reflect the short and long term economic benefits of the merger.
In present value terms the refund is worth about $248 million.
The directors of SBC and Pacific Telesis plan to evaluate the CPUC decision and decide whether to go through with the merger.
The final CPUC decision was sharply lower than the $590.5 million refund over five years proposed by two administrative law judges, who make recommendations to the commission.

SBC and Pacific Telesis had urged the California commissioners to reject the judges' proposal and approve the merger without conditions, saying the benefits of the merger would flow to ratepayers in the form of lower prices for telecommunications services. They said the merger would also boost the California economy because it would create new jobs.
Commissioners touted the economic benefits of the proposed merger, saying the combination of the two telephone companies would boost the economy and provide jobs.
"This will afford California a significant opportunity," Commissioner Richard Bilas said/ "There will be many beneficiaries: the merged companies, the ratepayers, (and the) stockholders."
Consumer groups had called for refunds to customers of nearly $1 billion over five years.
SBC and Pacific Telesis announced their merger plans last April. Shareholders from both companies approved the merger last summer.

The companies serve the nation's two most populous states -- California and Texas -- and seven of the nation's 10 largest metropolitan areas. Together, the two companies 1996 revenues totalled $23.5 billion.
The proposed merger was approved by a vote of four to one.
